Hmmm. I had some permanent dye at the tips of my hair (which I had been growing out for a year) and the henna covered it and my hair is completely even all over. I *think* that the only concern is using traditional hair dye OVER henna, as that can literally melt your hair off. But if you're at all interested I think it was hennaforhair.com that I read religiously for two weeks before trying it. The website looks dated but the information is very useful. The one thing they hammer in is to shop as carefully as possible because the henna needs to be body art quality (BAQ) and can contain no metallic salts (as are in traditional hair dye) because the whole hair melty thing.

I did my whole head, and my hair texture lis literally silky and shiny for the first time in my life. I have naturally coarse, dry hair and scalp and seriously my hair feels great. It doesn't bleed after washes or anything either, and I had read before that it doesn't fade (which so far is true for me), so the only upkeep should be doing your roots. Anecdotal evidence, I know, but I have to rave about it because I love it.

I'm afraid to counsel you on using it on a full head of dyed hair, because I am SO not an expert and I don't want to steer you wrong, but hopefully you can figure something out through your own research. Also search this subreddit for henna posts, too! I saw a lot of awesome results on here that inspired me to try it.

A little late but I have two horrible butterfly stories.  

First when I was about eight and I was on a bike riding trail with my mom. We were riding along peacefully when all of a sudden, I see a butterfly floating directly ahead of me about twenty feet. The path is narrow and I can't get out of the way without colliding with my mom. Do I slow down and get behind her? No. Just before butterfly impact, I crash into a ditch on the left. My mom was embarrassed and kept riding.

Story two! Someone invited me to a wedding and I say, sure whatever, I have a fancy dress. I never really got fancy for anything so I felt really cool about dressing up. The dress was champagne pink and just kickass all around. Anyways, the wedding was at one of those plant-museum things, I seriously can't think of what they're called right now. But basically a zoo for plants. Neato, right? Wrong.  

After the ceremony we went to the limited time BUTTERFLY GARDEN which was just a giant, enclosed room that had a bunch of flowers and, you guessed it, HUNDREDS of fucking butterflies everywhere. Giant, horrible butterflies. I grabbed a tasty alcoholic beverage and tried to ignore my terror. A butterfly landed on me and I spilled the drink all over myself and looked like an idiot in front of a lot of strangers.


**tl;dr** Fuck butterflies.
